title: Apartment Home Lease Catch-Up Amounts — Late Fees Carried
content:
The part of a late period's still-unpaid late fees that an Apartment Home Lease catch-up amount carries follows the lateness record:

- a lease on which no other billing period carries an initial late fee line dated in the last 12 months carries none of them;
- a lease on which exactly one other billing period does carries its still-unpaid late fees only up to the amount of the period's initial late fee line;
- any other lease — two or more other billing periods with an initial late fee line dated in the last 12 months — carries all of them.

The last 12 months means dated after the same day of the month twelve months before the handling date. The period's own initial late fee line is not counted as "another billing period". The period's still-unpaid late fees are its late fee lines, less the courtesy waiver and charge reversal credits posted for it, that remain unpaid once the period's payments have been applied.

## Worked cases (hypothetical)

Period: initial late fee line $90.00, daily late fee lines $40.00, still-unpaid late fees $130.00.

| Other billing periods with an initial late fee line in the last 12 months | Late fees carried |
|---|---|
| 0 | $0.00 |
| 1 | the lower of $130.00 and the initial line of $90.00: $90.00 |
| 2 | $130.00 |
| 3 | $130.00 |

Same period with only $60.00 of late fees still unpaid and exactly one other late period: the lower of $60.00 and $90.00, so $60.00.

**Window boundary.** Handling date 10 June 2026: another period's initial late fee line dated 11 June 2025 counts; one dated 10 June 2025 does not.
